claims.text: Đơn Hàng's own database stays single-shop at stage-3; the layouts run on lab databases: donhang_tenancy (shared tables in public, schemas shop_1/shop_2) and donhang_shop_1/donhang_shop_2 (a database per shop), all holding the same orders split by shop.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3: db/tenancy/*.sql, scripts/backend/tenancy-db.sh, STAGE.md; DECISIONS.md §3 2026-10-06 outline multitenancy-and-sharding

claims.text: A PostgreSQL schema is a named namespace inside one database that contains tables; same-named tables in two schemas (shop_1.orders, shop_2.orders) are separate. Every new database has a schema public, where tables created without a schema name go.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs: 5.10.1 Creating a Schema; 5.10.2 The Public Schema

claims.text: search_path is the ordered list of schemas PostgreSQL searches for a table name written without a schema; SET changes it for the current connection (session) only; after SET search_path TO shop_2 the name orders resolves to shop_2.orders.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs: 5.10.3 The Schema Search Path; SQL command SET (effect lasts until end of session)

claims.text: A schema-qualified name such as shop_1.orders refers to that schema's table regardless of search_path; a connection that never sets search_path uses the default "$user", public (public last; no donhang schema exists), so in donhang_tenancy orders is public.orders.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs: 5.10.3 The Schema Search Path (qualified names; default "$user", public)

claims.text: A PostgreSQL connection is made to one database; a query cannot read another database's tables, and naming one (donhang_shop_2.public.orders) gets ERROR: cross-database references are not implemented.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs: 22.1 Overview (Managing Databases); examples/don-hang @ stage-3 outputs/stage-3/scripts/backend/tenancy-models.txt

claims.text: In shared-schema.sql lines 9-29 @ stage-3, customers and orders have PRIMARY KEY (shop_id, id), orders has FOREIGN KEY (shop_id, customer_id) REFERENCES customers (shop_id, id) on line 27, and index orders_shop_id_customer_id (shop_id, customer_id) on line 29.

A composite foreign key (shop_id, customer_id) referencing customers (shop_id, id) makes PostgreSQL reject an order whose customer is not a row of the same shop; a key on (shop_id, id) lets each shop reuse id values from 1.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs: 5.5.5 Foreign Keys (multicolumn), 5.5.4 Primary Keys

claims.text: A B-tree index whose first column is shop_id lets a query with WHERE shop_id = X read only that shop's part of the index; an index not starting with shop_id cannot narrow a search to one shop by itself.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs: 11.3 Multicolumn Indexes; lesson backend.l2.composite-indexes

claims.text: schema-per-shop.sql @ stage-3 creates schemas shop_1 and shop_2, each with an orders table that has no shop_id column.

tenancy-models.sh @ stage-3: sql() (lines 11-13) wraps psql --host db, --dbname picks the database; lines 15-28 read shop 2's orders thrice (1 paid, 2 new); || true continues past the join error; lines 33-49 run ALTER TABLE ... gift_note in BEGIN/ROLLBACK per table.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3 scripts/backend/tenancy-models.sh lines 11-49; outputs/stage-3/scripts/backend/tenancy-models.txt; bash manual (|| list)

claims.text: Each layout step from shared tables to a database per shop gives stronger isolation (and a database per shop can be backed up on its own) at the cost of repeating migrations, connections and monitoring per shop; holds when shops are managed by one team on one code base.
claims.source_hint: general multi-tenant SaaS design reasoning; PostgreSQL docs pg_dump (dumps one database)

claims.text: Layouts can be mixed: when one shop is far larger than the rest, it can get its own database while small shops share tables, with the api choosing the connection by shop.
claims.source_hint: general multi-tenant design reasoning; outline item 6

claims.text: A database per shop should not be the default when there are many small shops, because per-shop repetition is a common source of failures; it is right when a contract requires separation or when there are few, large shops.
claims.source_hint: general multi-tenant design reasoning; opposing view stated in the same bullet

claims.text: When one migration runs per database, it can succeed on some shops' databases and not on others, leaving the api with tables of two different versions.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs: transactions are per database/connection (no cross-database transaction); backend.l1.migrations

claims.text: DonHang.Payments has its own database, donhang_payments, on the same PostgreSQL server as donhang at stage-3.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3 docker-compose.yml payments service; lesson backend.l3.payments-service
